newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul to summon 26 more politicians in Hanbo probe.
newsitem.headline: Seoul to summon 26 more politicians in Hanbo probe.

text.p: South Korean state prosecution plans to summon 26 more politicians this week for questioning over a bribery scandal surrounding the stricken Hanbo Group, state and other media reports said on Sunday.
They, including 13 current members of parliament, are part of the 33 politicians named by Hanbo founder Chung Tae-soo as having taken money from him.
Seven other politicians were interrogated by prosecutors late last week and most of them admitted taking money from Chung in what they called was "political funds".
Chung and nine others are on trial for bribery, while his son and Hanbo Group chairman Chung Bo-keun was jailed in late March for embezzlement of company funds.
The Korean Broadcasting System (KBS) radio reported five lawmakers who were sommoned on Saturday had been released by early Sunday after questioning overnight.
Prosecution officials could not be reached for comment.

Four of them were from the ruling New Korea Party, including Kim Deog-ryong, a member of President Kim Young-sam's inner circle and one of nine people widely tipped as the party's candidate in the presidential polls in December.
KBS and the Yonhap Television News quoted Kim Deog-ryong as telling reporters that he had been cleared of a suspecion that he took money from Chung Tae-soo.

The scandal, uncovered after the group's flagship Hanbo Steel Co folded in January under $5.8 billion of debts, revealed a web of corruption and influence-peddling involving top bankers and politicians.
Separately, a parliamentary inquiry started last week and has heard evidence from Chung Tae-soo, top bankers and a close associate of President Kim Young-sam.
Chung and his son Bo-keun will be in the spotlight on Monday when the younger Chung is due to testify before the parliamentary inquiry while his father stands trial.
